title: Iceland Cuts Electric-Car Grant and Lowers Price Ceiling From 1 November
dek: The passenger-car grant falls from ISK 500,000 to ISK 400,000, and cars priced above ISK 8 million no longer qualify. Support for vans and buses continues for businesses.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Electric cars plugged into public charging points

keyPoints: From November 1, the grant for eligible electric passenger cars falls by ISK 100,000, from ISK 500,000 to ISK 400,000.
The maximum price of an eligible passenger car falls from ISK 10 million to ISK 8 million.
The Ministry of the Environment, Energy and Climate signed the regulation and announced the change on October 14.
Support for vans, goods vehicles and buses continues, limited to companies and people actively operating a business.
body:
Iceland has reduced its purchase grant for electric passenger cars from November 1, and has lowered the price ceiling for eligible vehicles. Iceland Review reported the change, citing the Ministry of the Environment, Energy and Climate.

## What changed

The grant falls from ISK 500,000 to ISK 400,000. The maximum price of an eligible car drops from ISK 10 million to ISK 8 million, so cars costing more than ISK 8 million no longer qualify. Vans, goods vehicles and buses remain eligible, but only for companies and people actively operating a business.

The Environment and Energy Agency says applications approved on or after November 1, 2026 receive at most ISK 400,000. The rule is tied to the approval date of the application, not to when the car was bought or ordered. Buyers who want the older terms must have an application approved before that date and meet every condition of the grant.

## The government's reasoning

The ministry says electric-car grants had largely gone to higher-income groups in recent years. Lowering the maximum eligible price is meant to direct funding toward buyers in lower price ranges and to increase the number of such vehicles on the second-hand market. Officials point to the removal of excise duties on new electric cars on January 1, 2026, and argue that electric cars are now more competitive to buy and cheaper to run than petrol and diesel vehicles.

The Climate and Energy Fund's 2025 annual report found that direct grants for passenger cars and delivery vans produce considerably less benefit than many of the fund's other projects, according to the ministry. The new regulation also clarifies the fund's framework and streamlines how it announces and allocates competitive grants.

## What buyers should check

The announcement does not by itself establish an individual vehicle's eligibility. Applicants should check the fund's detailed conditions and the approval date of their application before committing to a purchase. Dealers have been promoting the deadline to customers, since the change applies to approvals rather than purchase dates.

## Charging is a separate question

The grant covers vehicle purchases, not access to chargers. Iceland Review has recently reported plans for 21 additional charging stations outside the capital area, and earlier coverage has examined slower electric-vehicle sales and registrations.
